subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:

Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Sara -- thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of the technical items we discussed and agreed actions so everyone is aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you shared:
- Real-time triage system requires median inference latency < 120ms for single-turn prompts during business hours (peak QPS ~1200 across region).
- Occasional batch scoring jobs (nightly) need throughput for up to 100k requests/hour with relaxed latency (~2s).
- Current self-hosted stack struggles with cold-start latency and inconsistent tail latency under burst load.

Goals agreed:
- Production SLO: 99th percentile latency <= 250ms during peak for primary inference flows; median target <= 120ms.
- Nightly batch jobs to be serviced via a separate fallback topology to avoid impacting real-time SLOs.
- Data controls: VPC peering + audit logs retained 13 months (SOC2 requirement).

Model & inference requirements:
- Primary model: multi-turn clinical coding assistant (decoder-only LLM, ~20B parameters) -- we discussed both quantized FP16 and 8-bit int variants.
- Tokenization: expected average prompt length 120 tokens, response ~60 tokens.
- KV-cache reuse for multi-turn sessions is important; must support warm cache affinity per user session.

Suggested deployment topology (high level):
1) Real-time tier: Dedicated instances with GPU pooling (NVIDIA H100 or equivalent), continuous batching window tuned to meet <120ms median while keeping 99p under 250ms.
2) Fallback tier: Cost-optimized quantized replicas for degraded mode and nightly batch jobs (separate worker queues).
3) Edge routing: Smart routing by region with automatic fallback to a secondary region (within same cloud provider) if capacity constrained.

Attachments I included: SLA proposal (redwood-sla-proposal.pdf), your topology worksheet (mediq-topology-reqs.xlsx) with the notes I took, and a quick topology sketch (topology-diagram.png).

Open questions / action items:
- Dev: confirm feasibility of hitting 99p<=250ms for the 20B model on your target instance types with sample traffic. (Dev, can you validate with a perf run?)
- Sara: confirm if the 13-month audit log retention is firm or flexible.
- Laura: I'll put together a canary/rollout plan tied to your release windows.

Next touchpoints:
- Dev will share initial perf numbers by EOD Thu 3/5 PST.
- We can schedule a short follow-up (30m) next week to review perf and pricing tradeoffs.

Thanks again -- Marissa

Sara / Marissa -- quick technical note from my side after a first pass: 
- We can expect median latency ~95-130ms on H100s with FP16 for the 20B model at a per-GPU batching config optimized for your 120 token prompts if we reserve dedicated pools. 99p depends heavily on burst shaping and session affinity; with warm KV-cache and prefetched contexts we should be able to get 99p <= 250ms in steady state.
- For nightly batch work, we'll route to quantized int8 replicas with autoscaling; throughput target of 100k reqs/hr is straightforward (will need autoscaling policies and larger worker clusters during the window).
- Cold-starts: recommend pre-warming minimum replica count during business hours and a small pool of hot-standbys to cut cold-start tail latency.

I'll run a microbenchmark against a synthetic workload tomorrow and upload the numbers to the Drive link. Attaching a short perf-plan: perf-plan.md (see Drive).
